description: Gezegenlerarası Hayatta Kalma Rehberi: Mars Haritası
summary: ARIADNE is an uncertainty-aware Mars EVA planning and rehearsal system. It turns terrain, consumables, communication delay and radiation risk into a live return margin: the time an astronaut still has to reach shelter safely. This margin becomes a clear red boundary on the map. Rover LiDAR and drone scouting can resolve unknown terrain and trigger replanning, while a replay of Curiosity’s 20 May 2024 radiation event demonstrates how quickly the safe area can contract. The project combines NASA and USGS planetary data, Python planning algorithms, ROS 2 and Gazebo robot simulation, and an Unreal Engine mission view. ARIADNE helps crews make time-critical local decisions without waiting for Earth, while preserving the difference between archived, derived, simulated and scenario data.
details:
ARIADNE supports the planning and rehearsal of a crewed Mars EVA at Boxwork-West in Gale crater. Its central output is a live “red line”: the boundary from which the crew can still return to shelter within the available oxygen, battery, walking-time and radiation constraints.

The system reads planetary product metadata instead of assuming Earth coordinates. A 1 m Gale terrain mosaic and HiRISE-derived products provide terrain context. The Python core calculates walking cost, return-time fields, consumable margins and safety boundaries. ROS 2 manages mission state, rules, sensor observations and robot commands. Gazebo is the physics and autonomy authority for the rover and scout drone, while Unreal Engine presents the astronaut-scale mission environment and telemetry.

Robot observations are treated as evidence rather than perfect simulator knowledge. Rover LiDAR and drone scouting can mark blocked or observed cells, update uncertainty and cause a new route to be generated. The science workflow also records sample identity, location, instrument context, quality and provenance. Archived NASA measurements remain distinct from derived, simulated and scenario data.

For the emergency demonstration, ARIADNE replays Curiosity RAD data from 20 May 2024. The recorded dose rate rose from approximately 5.7 to 351 µGy/h. At that time, Earth was about 15.8 light-minutes away, making a question-and-answer cycle roughly 32 minutes. ARIADNE therefore supports immediate local shelter and replanning decisions.

Tools: Python 3.12, ROS 2 Jazzy, Gazebo Harmonic, Unreal Engine 5, NumPy, GDAL/rasterio, NAIF SPICE and GitHub Actions., 3D models, music and voice work are disclosed in the repository; NASA measurements were not generated by AI.
